paper.core_task: Improving training stability and scalability of continuous-time consistency models for few-step image generation

contributions.name: A unified diffusion formulation combining EDM and Flow Matching
contributions.author_claim_text: Our first contribution is TrigFlow, a new formulation that unifies EDM (Karras et al., 2022;2024) and Flow Matching (Peluchetti, 2022;Lipman et al., 2022;Liu et al., 2022;Albergo et al., 2023;Heitz et al., 2023), significantly simplifying the formulation of diffusion models, the
contributions.description: TrigFlow is a new diffusion process formulation that simplifies EDM and Flow Matching into a unified framework with trigonometric coefficients, enabling simpler analysis and parameterization of diffusion and consistency models.

contributions.name: Techniques to stabilize continuous-time consistency model training
contributions.author_claim_text: Building on this foundation, we analyze the root causes of instability in CM training and propose a complete recipe for mitigation.
contributions.description: A set of theoretically motivated improvements including modified time conditioning, adaptive group normalization, re-formulated training objective with adaptive weighting and normalization, and progressive annealing to stabilize and scale continuous-time consistency model training.

contributions.name: Efficient Jacobian-vector product computation for Flash Attention
contributions.author_claim_text: To fill this gap, we propose a similar algorithm (detailed in Appendix F) that efficiently computes both softmax selfattention and its JVP in a single forward pass in the style of Flash Attention, significantly reducing GPU memory usage for JVP
contributions.description: An algorithm for computing both attention and its Jacobian-vector product in a single forward pass, enabling memory-efficient and stable tangent computation for large-scale continuous-time consistency model training.

novelty_claims.text: The proposed TrigFlow, as a novel unification of EDM and Flow Matching, substantially simplifies the analysis presented later and the practical techniques.

Model architecture modifications are original since existing works are mostly inherited from Diffusion Models' design and focus on the training techniques and formulations, leaving the architectural design underexplored.
The unified perspective on previous diffusion and flow-matching parameterizations is thorough, complete, and well-grounded, offering novel insights that could benefit the community.
Strategies for scaling such models to large sizes and datasets are proposed, namely JVP Rearrangement and JVP of Flash Attention.
